## Self-study: Units in python

As you may have noticed, numbers do not have a units in python. In science, all quantities need to be reported with and associated unit - ideally SI or with an appropriate prefix. In this course, we will represent units as a separate string variable that can be printed with the answer as shown below. This is also the format you should use for the exam.

#### (a) Unit as a string - examples

Length of an ideal H-bond:

```{python}

len_Hbond = 0.28
unit_len_Hbond = "nm"

print("An ideal H-bond is", len_Hbond, unit_len_Hbond) 

```

Molecular weight of human alcohol dehydrogenase:

```{python}

MW_ADH = 42
unit_MW_ADH = "kDa"

print("MW of ADH is", MW_ADH, unit_MW_ADH) 

```

Approximate diameter of human liver cell:

```{python}

diam_hlc = 30
unit_diam_hlc = "µm"

print("An typical liver cell is", diam_hlc, unit_diam_hlc, "wide") 

```
#### (b) Unit as a string - exercises

Convert to millimolar: 0.15 M
```{python}
conc = ...      # Replace ... with your code
unit_conc = "..."

print("The concentration is", conc, unit_conc) 
```

Convert to Å: 13.2 nm
```{python}
length = ...      # Replace ... with your code
unit_length = "..."

print("13.2 nm corresponds to", length, unit_length) 
```
